excerpts.text:
Article 53 of the [Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties](https://legal.un.org/ilc/texts/instruments/english/conventions/1_1_1969.pdf) (adopted May 1969, the VCLT) thus states:

> A treaty is void if, at the time of its conclusion, it conflicts with a peremptory norm of general international law. For the purposes of the present Convention, a peremptory norm of general international law is a norm accepted and recognized by the international community of States as a whole as a norm from which no derogation is permitted and which can be modified only by a subsequent norm of general international law having the same character.

excerpts.text:
VCLT Article 53 declares void any treaty that, at the time of its conclusion, conflicts with a [peremptory norm](/learn/glossary/peremptory-norm) of general international law ([jus cogens](/learn/glossary/jus-cogens)).

Article 53 of the Vienna Convention on the [Law of Treaties](/learn/glossary/law-of-treaties) ([VCLT](/learn/glossary/vclt)), 1969, codifies the [doctrine](/learn/glossary/doctrine) of *[jus cogens](/learn/glossary/jus-cogens)* — peremptory norms — within the [law of treaties](/learn/glossary/law-of-treaties).
